hazard: Lack of follow-up on mental health history

reports.title: Gary McDonald: Prevention of future deaths report

promises.quote: the Head of Healthcare has consulted with other stakeholders within the team about the concern raised and have considered ways this concern can be alleviated. The healthcare team have introduced an updated version (V4) of the EDiC pathway and passport. This
promises.summary: Introduced updated EDiC pathway version 4 with passport checklist to ensure follow-up on mental health history
promises.timescale: Day 5 - Initial Management Review and key word search undertaken by a Seniorurse

concerns.quote: During his initial healthcare screening appointment on the evening he arrived at HMP Hewell ( 25.3.21 ) and his secondary healthcare screening appointment the following day, Mr. McDonald denied any mental health issues, and denied any current thoughts of suicide or self-harm. His community GP records were 1 requested and were received by the prison on 30.3.21; these showed a previous history of depression, and two previous drug overdoses, the most recent of which had been only 7 months earlier

links.explanation: Both reports highlight that prisoners' known mental‑health risk information (GP records or PER) was not reviewed during initial healthcare screening, leading to missed follow‑up.
links.earlier_quote: During his initial healthcare screening appointment on the evening he arrived at HMP Hewell ( 25.3.21 ) and his secondary healthcare screening appointment the following day, Mr. McDonald denied any mental health issues, and denied any current thoughts of suicide or self-harm.
links.later_quote: the agency nurse who conducted the deceased's initial healthcare screening appointment on his arrival at HMP Hewell may not have looked at his PER, either because he did not have access to a copy of it, or because he had not been trained to ensure that he looked at it.
